issues.description: Constructor signature mismatch for class SealSaloon: the Problem Statement (UML and explicit text) requires a constructor SealSaloon(String) that accepts the saloon name and implies the name should be stored for identification. However, the provided Solution implements a no-argument constructor public SealSaloon() (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/SealSaloon.java line 8) and the Template/Main uses new SealSaloon() (template_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Main.java line 11). The template does not include a SealSaloon(String) constructor nor does the solution define or store a name field. This contradicts the specification and will confuse students which constructor to implement and whether a name field/getter is required.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor requirement consistent across artifacts. Options: (A) Update the Problem Statement to require a no-argument constructor (SealSaloon()) and remove the requirement to pass/store a name; or (B) Update the template and solution to implement public SealSaloon(String name), add a private final name field with a getter, and update Main to call new SealSaloon("<name>") where appropriate. Alternatively, provide both constructors (no-arg and String) and document the preferred one clearly in the statement so students are not left uncertain.
